docs.title: Project NexusPilot
docs.text:
NexusPilot is an open-source, modular Desktop Human-Grade Automation Suite delivered as a cross-compatible Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server and an Antigravity Plugin + Skill.

It provides AI agents with human-like vision, mouse control, keyboard input, and native Windows accessibility perception, enabling autonomous operation of native desktop software.

flowchart TD
    subgraph AgentLayer["Agent Layer (MCP Clients)"]
        A1["Google Antigravity"]
        A2["Claude Code"]
        A3["Cursor / Windsurf"]
    end

    subgraph PluginLayer["NexusPilot Plugin & Skill Layer"]
        B1["SKILL.md (Observe-Plan-Act-Verify)"]
        B2["Safety Guardrails & Boundary Checks"]
    end

    subgraph MCPEngine["NexusPilot MCP Engine (Local Daemon)"]
        C1["Tool Dispatcher (JSON-RPC)"]
        C2["Perception Engine (MSS / DWM Cropping)"]
        C3["Semantic Engine (Windows UI Automation COM)"]
        C4["Actuation Engine (Win32 SendInput / DPI V2)"]
        C5["Failsafe Guardian (Corner Slam / Boundary Lock)"]
    end

    subgraph WindowsOS["Host Operating System (Windows 10 / 11)"]
        D1["Display Surfaces & Window Handles (HWND)"]
        D2["Mouse & Keyboard Event Queue"]
        D3["UI Automation Core (UIAutomationCore.dll)"]
    end

    AgentLayer --> PluginLayer
    PluginLayer --> MCPEngine
    MCPEngine --> WindowsOS

docs.title: Key Highlights
docs.text:
• Dual-Modal Perception: Combines sub-30ms screen capture with the Windows UI Automation (UIA) accessibility tree for 100% coordinate precision.
  • DPI-Aware Win32 Actuation: Low-level SendInput mouse and keyboard control with Per-Monitor DPI v2 normalization.
  • Hardware Corner Failsafe: Slamming the physical mouse cursor to (0, 0) immediately halts all automation.
  • Cross-Agent Compatible: Works out-of-the-box with Google Antigravity, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf via standard MCP.

docs.title: Win32 Actuation Engine & Kinematics
docs.text: NexusPilot dispatches low-level mouse and keyboard events directly into the Windows OS event queue using native Win32 SendInput.

docs.title: 1. Per-Monitor DPI v2 Awareness
docs.text:
Multi-monitor setups with varying scale factors (e.g., 4K primary at 150% and 1080p secondary at 100%) often cause coordinate drift in automation tools.

NexusPilot explicitly registers Per-Monitor DPI Awareness v2 via SetProcessDpiAwareness(2): - Maps virtual screen space across all connected displays (SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN, SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN, SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN, SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN). - Normalizes pixel coordinates to Win32 absolute units ($0 \text{ to } 65535$) using MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE | MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK.

docs.title: 2. Window Focus Stealing Prevention
docs.text:
Windows blocks background processes from rudely bringing windows to the foreground. NexusPilot implements the standard Win32 focus handshake:

  1. Identifies the foreground thread via GetWindowThreadProcessId(GetForegroundWindow()).
  2. Attaches thread input: AttachThreadInput(foreThread, appThread, TRUE).
  3. Calls ShowWindow(targetHwnd, SW_RESTORE) to un-minimize if needed.
  4. Executes SetForegroundWindow and BringWindowToTop.
  5. Detaches thread input cleanly.

docs.title: 3. Human-Grade Mouse Kinematics
docs.text:
• Bézier Trajectories: Eases mouse movements over 5-10 intermediate waypoints to avoid triggering rapid-jitter UI glitches.
  • Full Drag-and-Drop: Emits synchronized MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTDOWN, intermediate drag motions, and MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTUP.
  • Unicode Keystroke Typing: Uses KEYEVENTF_UNICODE so international characters, emojis, and symbols type reliably regardless of the host keyboard layout.

docs.title: Dual-Modal Perception Architecture
docs.text:
Traditional vision-only computer-use agents rely solely on raw screenshots. This approach leads to high coordinate hallucination, breaks under Windows DPI scaling (125%/150%), and incurs large token overhead.

NexusPilot solves this by implementing a dual-modal perception stream:

flowchart LR
    A["Target Application Window"]
    A -->|Visual Stream| B["Fast Screen Capture\n(MSS + DWM Window Cropping)"]
    A -->|Semantic Stream| C["Windows UIAutomation COM\n(Exact Control Coordinates)"]
    B --> D["Vision LLM Fallback"]
    C --> E["Deterministic 1-Click Actuation"]

docs.title: 1. The Semantic Stream (Windows UI Automation)
docs.text:
NexusPilot interfaces with Windows UIAutomationCore.dll via typed COM client wrappers:

  • Exact Bounding Boxes: Extracts [x, y, width, height] and center points directly from the operating system accessibility tree.
  • Zero Coordinate Guessing: The agent clicks click_element(query="Save") rather than estimating pixels.
  • Token Efficiency: A semantic tree representation costs ~300 to 500 tokens, saving 70%+ compared to streaming full-screen images.

docs.title: 2. The Visual Stream (Screen Capture Engine)
docs.text:
When an application renders on a custom canvas (DirectX, Electron canvas, game engines) where semantic accessibility nodes are absent, the visual stream takes over:

  • Sub-30ms Capture: Uses mss for high-throughput screen grabs.
  • DWM Extended Frame Bounds: Queries DwmGetWindowAttribute with DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS (flag 9) to eliminate the invisible 7-pixel drop shadow padding found in standard Win32 GetWindowRect.
  • Targeted Window Cropping: Crops directly to the active application window bounding box, preserving privacy and reducing tokens.

docs.title: Safety Guardian & Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards
docs.text: Autonomous desktop actuation requires strict safety guardrails to protect user privacy and prevent destructive mistakes.

docs.title: 1. Hardware Corner Failsafe
docs.text:
NexusPilot monitors physical mouse cursor coordinates prior to executing any synthetic actuation:

  • Trigger: Slamming the physical mouse cursor into the top-left corner (0, 0) immediately halts all automation.
  • Enforcement: Any in-flight or subsequent MCP tool call aborts with safety_abort: true.
  • Reset: The failsafe remains locked until the user explicitly calls reset_safety_failsafe or approves resumption.

docs.title: 2. Application Boundary Isolation
docs.text:
To prevent an AI agent from accidentally clicking into personal messaging apps (Slack, WhatsApp, Discord) or browser password vaults:

  • Hard Boundary Lock: set_safety_boundary(enabled=True, hwnd=...) locks clicks strictly within the target window's bounding rectangle [left, top, right, bottom].
  • Coordinates outside this rectangle raise a SafetyViolationError and are immediately blocked.

docs.title: 3. High-Risk Confirmation Gates
docs.text:
The Safety Guardian inspects typed text and clicked control labels against potentially irreversible keywords:

  • format, drop database, drop table, rm -rf, commit to production, push --force, delete from, kill -9

If detected, the engine flags high_risk_detected: true and requests explicit Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) confirmation before proceeding.

docs.title: Installation & Environment Setup
docs.text: NexusPilot runs locally on Windows 10 and 11 workstations without requiring external cloud containers.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Operating System: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit)
  • Python: Python 3.10+ installed and on system PATH
  • Permissions: Standard user permissions (Administrator rights optional, but recommended for testing with elevated developer tools)

docs.title: 2. Automated 1-Click Installation
docs.text:
Run the universal agent installer script:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File nexus-pilot/scripts/install-agents.ps1

Or double-click nexus-pilot/install-agents.bat in Windows Explorer.

The installer will: 1. Detect your local Python binary. 2. Install dependencies from nexus-pilot/requirements.txt. 3. Configure MCP settings for Antigravity, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf.

docs.title: 3. Manual Installation via Pip
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/nishantshaligram/NexusPilot.git
cd NexusPilot
pip install --user -r nexus-pilot/requirements.txt

docs.title: 4. Run Environment Diagnostic
docs.text:
Verify your display setup, DPI scale, and COM accessibility core:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File nexus-pilot/scripts/verify-environment.ps1

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: Get your AI agent to pilot a native desktop application in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Verify Health from CLI
docs.text:
Before connecting your agent, test the MCP engine directly from PowerShell:

python -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'nexus-pilot/server')
from input_synthesizer import InputSynthesizer
from uia_bridge import UIABridge

synth = InputSynthesizer()
print('Active Window:', synth.get_active_window()['title'])

bridge = UIABridge()
tree = bridge.inspect_ui_tree(max_depth=2)
print(f'Detected {len(tree[\"elements\"])} interactive UI controls on screen!')
"

docs.title: 2. Example Agent Prompts
docs.text: Once NexusPilot is enabled in your agent (Antigravity, Claude, or Cursor), try these real-world instructions:

docs.title: A. Windows Calculator Automation
docs.text: "Open Windows Calculator, click 7, click multiply, click 8, click equals, and verify the displayed result."

docs.title: B. Notepad Note Creation
docs.text: "Open Notepad, type 'Hello from NexusPilot', and save the file to my Desktop as test.txt."

docs.title: C. Developer Thick Client Navigation
docs.text: "Bring DBeaver to the front, click Test Connection, and tell me if the database ping succeeded."

docs.title: 3. The Emergency Stop
docs.text: If an agent ever makes an unintended action: - Slam your physical mouse into the top-left corner (0, 0). - NexusPilot will immediately trigger the hardware failsafe, halt input, and notify the agent to abort.

docs.title: Google Antigravity Integration
docs.text: NexusPilot is bundled as an official Antigravity plugin and skill.

docs.title: Installation in Antigravity
docs.text:
Copy the nexus-pilot folder to your global Antigravity plugins directory:

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$HOME\.gemini\config\plugins" -Force
Copy-Item -Path "nexus-pilot\*" -Destination "$HOME\.gemini\config\plugins\nexus-pilot" -Recurse -Force

Antigravity automatically discovers: 1. Plugin Manifest: plugin.json (author, logo, starter prompts) 2. MCP Server: mcp_config.json running server/pilot_server.py 3. Agent Skill: skills/desktop-human-pilot/SKILL.md 4. Safety Rules: rules/AGENTS.md (active globally while the plugin is enabled)

docs.title: Managing the Plugin
docs.text: You can toggle or inspect the plugin in the Antigravity UI: - Open customization://nexus-pilot in the Customizations page. - All 13 MCP tools (capture_screen, click_element, mouse_click, etc.) are available directly in your chat sessions.

docs.title: Claude Integration (Code CLI & Desktop)
docs.text: NexusPilot connects seamlessly to Anthropic's Claude Code CLI and Claude Desktop on Windows.

docs.title: 1. Claude Code CLI
docs.text:
Add the server to your global Claude CLI config (~/.claude.json) or project .mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nexus-pilot": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["F:/Personal/ComputerUse/nexus-pilot/server/pilot_server.py"]
    }
  }
}

Or add via the CLI: 

claude mcp add nexus-pilot python "F:/Personal/ComputerUse/nexus-pilot/server/pilot_server.py"

docs.title: 2. Claude Desktop App
docs.text:
Open your Claude Desktop configuration file at %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nexus-pilot": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["F:/Personal/ComputerUse/nexus-pilot/server/pilot_server.py"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop. The hammer icon will display the NexusPilot desktop tools.

docs.title: Cursor & Windsurf Integration
docs.text: Configure NexusPilot inside Cursor or Windsurf IDE.

docs.title: 1. Cursor IDE
docs.text:
1. Open Cursor Settings (Ctrl + ,).
  2. Navigate to Features $\rightarrow$ MCP Servers.
  3. Click Add New MCP Server:
  4. Name: nexus-pilot
  5. Type: command
  6. Command: python F:/Personal/ComputerUse/nexus-pilot/server/pilot_server.py

Or add directly to ~/.cursor/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nexus-pilot": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["F:/Personal/ComputerUse/nexus-pilot/server/pilot_server.py"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 2. Windsurf (Codeium)
docs.text:
Add to ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nexus-pilot": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["F:/Personal/ComputerUse/nexus-pilot/server/pilot_server.py"]
    }
  }
}
Reload the IDE window to activate the tools.

docs.title: MCP Tools Reference
docs.text: Complete specification of all tools exposed by the NexusPilot MCP server.

docs.title: capture_screen
docs.text: Captures high-resolution desktop or window screenshot. - Arguments: - monitor_index (int, default 0): Physical monitor index. - window_title (str, optional): Target window name for automatic cropping. - crop_rect (list[int], optional): [x, y, width, height] region of interest. - max_dimension (int, default 1920): Maximum width/height to limit token size. - Returns: { image_base64: str, width: int, height: int, dpi_scale: float }

docs.title: inspect_ui_tree
docs.text: Traverses the Windows UI Automation accessibility tree. - Arguments: - window_title (str, optional): Target window title. - max_depth (int, default 3): Traversal depth. - interactive_only (bool, default true): Filters for interactive controls (Buttons, Text boxes, Menus). - Returns: { elements: Array<{ name, control_type, id, rect, center }> }

docs.title: find_element
docs.text: Searches for a specific control by name, label, or automation ID. - Arguments: - query (str): Search keyword. - window_title (str, optional): Target window. - Returns: { found: bool, element: { name, rect, center, ... } }

docs.title: click_element
docs.text: Deterministically clicks a control by semantic name or automation ID. - Arguments: - query (str): Control name or ID. - window_title (str, optional): Target window title. - button (str, default "left"): "left", "right", or "middle". - clicks (int, default 1): Number of clicks. - Returns: { success: bool, clicked_element: str, coordinates: [x, y] }

docs.title: mouse_click
docs.text: Sends raw coordinate clicks via Win32 SendInput. - Arguments: x (int), y (int), button (str), clicks (int).

docs.title: mouse_drag
docs.text: Performs a smoothed drag-and-drop gesture. - Arguments: start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y, speed_ms.

docs.title: mouse_scroll
docs.text: Simulates mouse wheel scrolling. - Arguments: direction ("up" or "down"), amount (int), x (optional), y (optional).

docs.title: send_keystrokes
docs.text: Sends Unicode text typing or modifier hotkey chords. - Arguments: - text (str, optional): Unicode string to type. - keys (list[str], optional): Key combination (e.g. ['ctrl', 'shift', 'p']). - delay_ms (int, default 10): Inter-key delay in milliseconds.

docs.title: focus_window
docs.text: Restores and brings a window to the foreground with Win32 focus handshake. - Arguments: title_keyword (str).

docs.title: get_active_window
docs.text: Returns active window details (title, hwnd, pid, process_name, rect, dpi_scale).

docs.title: set_safety_boundary
docs.text: Locks click actuation exclusively within target window bounds. - Arguments: enabled (bool), hwnd (int, optional).

docs.title: reset_safety_failsafe
docs.text: Clears the emergency stop flag so automation can resume.

docs.title: check_health
docs.text: Verifies screen metrics, cursor position, UIA COM status, and active safety guards.
